item.title: Famed climber Nirmal Purja among 10 missing on Pakistan peak; 4 bodies recovered
item.description: Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing on Pakistan's Broad Peak located four bodies and were looking for the others, officials said. Acclaimed climber Nirmal Purja was among the missing.

item.title: U.S. investigating if Iran was behind cyberattack on Minnesota water systems
item.description: Malicious cyber activity affected technology at more than 30 community water systems across Minnesota this week, leading authorities to dig into whether Iranian actors are behind the attack, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Spain deploys military to Morocco border after migrant crossings; 34 deaths
item.description: At least 34 migrants died trying to reach the Spanish territory of Ceuta. Tens of thousands of people breached the frontier with Morocco and poured into the tiny Spanish territory.

item.title: U.S. investigating whether Iran hacked dozens of water systems
item.description: The U.S. is investigating whether Iran hacked more than 30 community water systems across Minnesota, CBS News has learned. Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: FIFA official resigns in protest of World Cup investment plan
item.description: The pressure is rising on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to ditch a $20 billion privatization plan, but soccer's governing body is doubling down and criticizing the media.

item.title: Trump's surprising announcement on Gaza includes claim that Hamas will disarm
item.description: President Trump says Hamas has agreed to enter the next phase of the Gaza peace deal, which will apparently include the disarmament of the militant group. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Stunning video shows migrants crossing Spain's border with Morocco
item.description: Spain has deployed its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants rushed the border with Morocco, leading to more than a dozen deaths, according to the Spanish News Agency EFE. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Sheriff at heart of Nancy Guthrie disappearance investigation shares new details on case
item.description: Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos, who has led the local investigation into Nancy Guthrie's disappearance, spoke to CBS News' Jonathan Vigliotti and revealed more details on the probe.

item.title: Iran claims strikes on ships in Strait of Hormuz and U.S. base in Kuwait
item.description: Iran says it targeted U.S. facilities in Kuwait and struck two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that were under "aerial escort" from the U.S.

item.title: New poll shows many Americans don't see economic relief from either Republican, Democratic parties
item.description: A recent CBS News poll shows many Americans feel Republicans and Democrats are hurting their cost of living. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto and Aaron Navarro report.

item.title: Netflix sued for allegedly losing unreleased Nicolas Cage movie
item.description: Lawsuit alleges that a drive storing $45 million spy film starring Nicolas Cage was "stolen right off a Netflix desk."

item.title: Trump says Hamas agreed to next phase of Gaza peace deal, including disarmament
item.description: President Trump said Hamas and his international "Board of Peace" have agreed on the next steps in a peace deal that includes Hamas' disarmament in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: Why Trump says he may pull his Todd Blanche attorney general nomination
item.description: President Trump says he may pull his attorney general nomination as Todd Blanche's future remains in limbo. CBS News' Taurean Small explains.

item.title: Trump says Hamas has agreed to next phase of the Gaza peace deal
item.description: President Trump says Hamas, the Iran-backed militant group in Gaza, has agreed to the next phase of the peace deal offered last fall to end the war between Israel and Hamas. CBS News' Courtney Kealy reports.

item.title: Democrats demand training info on ICE agent who killed immigrant in Maine
item.description: Two Democrats are demanding details and records about the training of an ICE officer who shot and killed a Colombian immigrant in Maine, according to a letter obtained by CBS News.

item.title: People with disabilities fear service cuts as DOJ questions legal protections
item.description: The Department of Justice in June issued a legal opinion saying states aren't required to provide services that help people with disabilities remain in their homes.

item.title: Iran conflict expands as Senate again rejects effort to limit Trump's war powers
item.description: A vote in the Senate to limit President Trump's war powers has narrowly failed again. Three Republicans voted in favor of it.

item.title: Ukrainian ambassador tracks how Kyiv's relationship with D.C. has evolved
item.description: The outgoing Ukrainian ambassador to the U.S. says Ukraine has been able to combat what she said characterized as a prior, erroneous narrative that Russia was winning the war, now in its fifth year​.

item.title: Anthropic reveals Claude "gained unauthorized access" to "real-world systems"
item.description: Anthropic's artificial intelligence model Claude "gained unauthorized access" to three outside organizations on three separate occasions during testing.

item.title: Trump says he may pull Blanche's nomination until 2 Senate critics leave office
item.description: President Trump said Todd Blanche will remain acting attorney general as a holdup on his nomination continues.

item.title: Pentagon weighs eliminating civilian tenure at military academies, draft memo says
item.description: The Pentagon is considering a sweeping remake of military higher education, including an end to civilian tenure and a "line-by-line" review of courses, according to a draft memo obtained by CBS News.

item.title: What the fires burning near Bordeaux's vineyards could mean for France's wine industry
item.description: In France, wildfires this summer have already burned an area four times the size of Paris, driving hundreds of thousands of people from their homes.

item.title: Hair sample from Nancy Guthrie's home inconclusive as search hits 6-month mark
item.description: A hair sample found at the home of Nancy Guthrie came back inconclusive after undergoing testing, Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos revealed Thursday.

item.title: Stolen Civil War-era cannonballs found in suitcase at Alabama airport
item.description: Law enforcement officials say a set of stolen Civil War-era cannonballs was discovered in a passenger's suitcase during a routine security screening at Alabama's Gulf Shores International Airport.

item.title: 7/30: CBS Evening News
item.description: Mass migration triggers a military response in the Spanish city of Ceuta; a powerful explosion destroys an Ohio home.

item.title: Father of Apalachee High School shooter sentenced to 15 years in prison
item.description: Colin Gray gets 15 years in prison after emotional sentencing hearing in Apalachee High School shooting case.

item.title: North American nations join Europe's, reject FIFA head's World Cup investment plan
item.description: North America's soccer body on Thursday rejected FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity investors, joining European nations in opposition.

item.title: European teams boycott FIFA over plan to sell World Cup stake to investors
item.description: A source close to Joshua Kushner's firm tells CBS News there's no politics behind FIFA's bid to draw private investment, but Europe's soccer powerhouses are crying foul.

item.title: Saudi, Israeli leaders try to shape Trump's decisions on Iran conflict
item.description: As conflict potentially expands in the region, Trump met with the Saudi defense minister and with Benjamin Netanyahu. The Israeli prime minister counseled Trump on three options for the war.

item.title: Lawyer, 42, tries on a different suit, gives lifeguarding a try: "Best summer of my life"
item.description: Ben Schweer, a medical malpractice lawyer from Pittsburgh, tried on a different summer suit, becoming a lifeguard at Delaware's Rehoboth Beach. Mark Strassmann has the story.
